neighbours.label: ' a' (or the modifier after it) where an abstract relational noun is expected: 'there is somewhat/something of a [gap / tension / trade-off] between …'
fire: There is something of a gap between what the law says and what the courts do.
This leaves somewhat of a mismatch between supply and demand in the region.
There is somewhat of a divide between the older and the newer members.
This creates somewhat of a tension between the two goals of the policy.
There remains something of a contrast between the northern and southern dialects.
This causes something of a delay between the order and the delivery.
There is a trade-off between battery life and screen brightness.
This sets up something of a conflict between the board and the founders.
quiet: She bought a wooden table for the kitchen at the weekend market.
He carried a heavy suitcase up the stairs of the old hotel.
My uncle is a bit of a joker at family dinners.
The children found a small frog beside the pond behind the school.
They rented a blue van to move the furniture across town.
He turned out to be more of a singer than a dancer.
The chef added a pinch of salt to the soup before serving.
We watched a long film about penguins on Saturday night.

notes: Card flags the pole broad (1.1% of tokens reach 0.1 of max). The output promotes ' order', ' bottleneck', ' gap', ' contrast', ' cycle', ' chain'. Probes: 'There is somewhat of a' 0.78, 'creates something of a' 0.78, 'start of a [cycle]' 0.43, 'a trade-off' 0.41; 'has become somewhat of a' 0.25, 'a bit of a' 0.11, 'bought a red bicycle' 0.01. So the lead-in matters, not only 'of a'.
